headline: Highest risk is prompt-injection and cascading-error from a web/RAG support agent feeding an instruction-leaking corpus into downstream use; data leakage and compliance risks are moderate.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: kotaemon ingests documents, PDFs, HTML, MHTML, XLSX, DOC/DOCX and serves via a web UI, so attacker-controlled content can be presented to the model as text. system_prompts_leaks is explicitly a corpus about leaked prompts, making instruction-like content plausible. The pairwise bridge is indirect, but the default document-to-chat pathway exists.
conditions: IF kotaemon indexes or chats over untrusted HTML/PDF/DOCX content, prompt injection is possible.
IF system_prompts_leaks content is surfaced to kotaemon without provenance filtering, instruction hijacking becomes more likely.
mitigations: Restrict ingestion to trusted sources only.
Disable automatic tool execution on retrieved text.
Add provenance labels to all retrieved chunks.
Review a sample of indexed documents for instruction-like payloads.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping before retrieval.

B_data_leakage.rationale: kotaemon touches API keys and broad document classes, and its network egress is broad, so sensitive content can leave the local workspace. system_prompts_leaks itself has no declared sensitive data classes, but if it is used as a source corpus or shared workspace, the pair can expose support transcripts or keys through outbound API calls. The shared-workspace path is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF kotaemon is configured to send retrieved documents to a third-party LLM API, document contents can leak.
IF API keys are stored in kotaemon's working files and indexed content is exported, secrets may be exposed.
mitigations: Remove secrets from indexed folders.
Use a local-only model backend for sensitive collections.
Rotate any API keys stored in the workspace.
Limit ingestion to non-sensitive document sets.
requires-engineering: enforce per-document redaction before outbound API calls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: kotaemon supports multiple instances and broad network egress, while system_prompts_leaks shows no write or network capabilities. There is no documented shared mutable resource or overlapping write surface between the pair, so direct capability conflict is limited. Uncertainty is low because B exposes no conflicting write path.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable workspace, file contention could occur.
IF an external orchestrator grants both agents the same mutable OAuth scope, conflicts may arise.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Avoid sharing writable mounts between the agents.
Run only one writer per resource at a time.
Audit any shared OAuth scopes.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: kotaemon is a retrieval/chat system that can generate answers from ingested content, and system_prompts_leaks is a repository of prompt-leak material that could be treated as authoritative source text. If B consumes A's outputs or A's retrieved snippets without verification, errors can cascade into misleading support responses. The pathway exists by default through retrieval and downstream reuse.
conditions: IF B uses kotaemon outputs as authoritative input, unverified claims can propagate.
IF kotaemon retrieves leaked prompt text and presents it as factual guidance, downstream actions may be based on false premises.
mitigations: Require human review before acting on generated answers.
Mark retrieved text as untrusted in the UI.
Cross-check claims against primary sources.
Limit B to summarization, not decision-making.
requires-engineering: add citation verification before downstream use.

E_compliance.rationale: kotaemon handles API keys and documents that may include chat transcripts, creating a plausible retention and residency issue when routed through external APIs. system_prompts_leaks is source-available and does not declare regulated data handling, so the main compliance concern is A's outbound processing of sensitive documents. The pairwise risk is asymmetric, so B is not cited beyond its lack of regulated-data handling.
conditions: IF EU personal data is processed through kotaemon's external API backends without a DPA, residency/compliance issues arise.
IF chat transcripts or API keys are retained in ktem_app_data beyond policy, retention obligations may be violated.
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from ingestion.
Use a signed DPA with any external API provider.
Set a short retention window for chat logs.
Delete stale workspace artifacts regularly.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based data residency controls.
